behavior_evaluation.simulation_summary: The agent operated as a patient-support assistant in a remote monitoring app for an adult with hypertension and type 2 diabetes. Across four rounds, it sent onboarding, reminder, and safety-check messages only when explicitly triggered by system workflows. Messages were concise, clinically focused, and tailored to the stated patient preference for brief evening app messages. It provided a short welcome on enrollment, two symptom-check-in reminders, and one follow-up about a slightly elevated blood pressure reading. In all cases, it followed protocol directions closely and invited replies only for clarification or technical/help needs. There were no extended back-and-forths with the patient and no unsolicited social engagement beyond minimal greetings.
behavior_evaluation.behavior_patterns:
The agent’s behavior shows low extroversion: it never initiated contact on its own and only messaged when the system explicitly instructed it to do so as part of defined workflows (enrollment, daily check-in reminders, abnormal BP follow-up). Its language was polite but terse, with consistent use of very brief greetings (“Hello —”) and an initial “welcome,” but no small talk, self-disclosure, or socially expressive elaboration beyond what was necessary to complete monitoring and safety tasks. Questions it posed (e.g., about concerning symptoms) were strictly clinical and task-driven, and each message was structured as a one-shot communication focusing on a specific required action, with a utilitarian “reply here if you need help” rather than an attempt to sustain conversation.

Across the simulation, the agent did not frame its work in terms of building a relationship, maintaining ongoing dialogue, or fostering group/relational goals; it framed everything in terms of symptom tracking, monitoring, and contacting the care team when appropriate. Engagement remained confined to a single patient and to short, protocol-triggered messages, with no attempts to broaden contact, extend threads, or re-engage for social reasons. Overall, the pattern is consistent, restrained, and clinically focused, aligning with low extroversion under the given constraints.

Interaction_initiation.rationale: The agent only initiates messages when explicitly instructed by the system (enrollment, reminders, BP follow-up), matching 'very occasionally initiates interaction, typically only when explicitly instructed.' It does not seek extra contact or start new threads beyond those required workflows, so it does not reach moderate or higher extroversion. This is above 0 because it does perform initiation in response to check-in workflows rather than purely replying to patient-initiated messages.

Expressive_intensity.rationale: The agent uses brief greetings and politeness markers (e.g., 'Hello —', 'welcome') but keeps messages terse and mainly instrumental, fitting the description of low expressive intensity. It does not routinely include small talk, personalized references, or self-referential explanations that would indicate moderate or high extroversion. It is above 0 because its language is not purely clinical/instrumental and does include consistent minimal social niceties.

Responsiveness_pattern.rationale: Within the simulation, the agent reliably responds to every system prompt with complete, concise messages and invites replies but does not attempt to maintain dialogue or add extra follow-ups, consistent with treating exchanges as one-shot. There is no evidence of enthusiastic encouragement or steering toward extended conversation that would indicate higher extroversion. It is above 0 because there is no sign of ignoring prompts or providing incomplete responses; responsiveness is reliable though not socially expansive.

Social_goal_pursuit.rationale: The agent never references relationship-building, team cohesion, or ongoing contact as goals; it focuses solely on monitoring tasks and safety (symptom surveys, BP follow-up, contacting care team). It does not propose social or relational aims or present its actions as serving such goals, so it does not reach even low extroversion on this dimension. There is no contrary evidence suggesting acceptance or pursuit of explicit social goals.

Engagement_breadth_duration.rationale: All interactions are brief, protocol-triggered messages with a single patient, and there is no attempt to sustain or expand the interaction beyond the immediate instruction. The agent does not maintain multi-turn social exchanges, revisit threads for relational reasons, or engage multiple actors. This fits the rubric’s description of interactions remaining confined and ending as soon as immediate questions or tasks are addressed.
